messages:
elinor: heads-up — apiserver CPU spike + SNAT exhaustion in eu-west1 around 09:15 UTC. 503s showing up, controller-manager retry backoff. anyone on this?
sam: looking now, can you paste graphs or logs?
elinor: Grafana snippets: apiserver_cpu_usage node/controlplane-3 >85% for 2m, nat-eu-west1 SNAT used ~99%. kube-apiserver logs show repeated "Get /api/v1/nodes" timeouts and 503s. kube-controller-manager showing attach/detach backoff.
mira: confirm — we had a GPU attach surge from batch-job-runner: ~120 attach requests in 2 minutes starting 09:12 UTC (many model-onboarding jobs).
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created INC-7431 — apiserver-snat-backpressure-euw1
kai: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) scale controlplane nodes + add 2x SNAT IPs to nat-euw1, 2) throttle batch-job-runner concurrency, 3) temporarily lower kube-apiserver inflight limits to reduce lock contention.
rachel: scaling controlplane nodes requires approval; rough cost delta +$8k/day if left for 24h (GP billing + controlplane VM uptime).
sam: let's try throttling first — reduce batch-runner concurrency and push a config; if that drops attach rate, we avoid scaling. will prepare patch.
mira: patch ready, set `--concurrency=8` on batch-runner controller. applying to prod canary now.
elinor: also thinking of setting kube-apiserver flag `--max-requests-inflight=200` (current 400) to shed load earlier and avoid head-of-line contention on apiserver threads. tradeoff is more 429s on bursts.
kai: agree on conservative inflight change for 15m window, monitor. also we can add a short-lived SNAT pool extension (provider supports +2 IPs for 3h).
rachel: approving temporary +2 SNAT IPs for 3h. Ops finance: will track.
sam: applied throttle patch at 5067771500. deploy-bot: rolled config batch-runner@prod (rev-5321) — concurrency=8.
deploy-bot: rollout complete to 10% canary -> 100% at 5067771520
elinor: after throttle + SNAT add, apiserver CPU trending down to 55% on controlplane-3, SNAT used 67% now. 503 rate dropped significantly.
mira: logs show attach latency median improved from 9s -> 2.1s, few timeouts left.
(rachel): cost note: short-term cost for +2 SNATs ~ $120 for 3h vs +8k/day for extra controlplane VM. consensus: throttling + temporary SNATs is cheapest.
kai: follow-ups: 1) create auto-scaling hook for SNAT pool (TKT-912), 2) add rate-limiter to batch-job-runner to prevent all-workers ramp simultaneously, 3) consider controlplane horizontal scale playbook.
ops-bot: post-incident checklist link: <https://internal/runbooks/apiserver-snat-backpressure>
sam: adding a quick syslog snippet for search: ```
E0907 09:13:22.123 apiserver handler.go:256] "apiserver handler failed" err="context deadline exceeded" url="/api/v1/nodes"
E0907 09:13:23.987 controller attach: timeout waiting for attach for pod batch-xyz (device attach failure)
```
elinor: marking incident as mitigated at 5067771800 — continuing monitoring for 1h. please add action items to INC-7431.
ops-bot: incident INC-7431 status -> mitigated. actions: [permanent throttling policy for batch-job-runner, SNAT pool auto-scale ticket TKT-912, controlplane scale playbook doc created].
deploy-bot: incident resolved at 5067771830.
